title: Emmy Noether: Modern LaTeX Working Corpus and Multilingual Translation Readers
description:
This is the reader-facing Emmy Noether working record for the Modern LaTeX Editions of Mathematics Manuscripts project. It contains modern LaTeX working editions, source-control material, and multilingual working translations; it is not a critical edition.

German and English: the record continues to front the 466-page v26/R823 German source-control reader. It retains the inherited RA10 English cumulative reader, standalone English Papers 01-43, and twelve bounded English components synchronized to R823. The full English reader is not globally synchronized to R823.

Spanish: the 473-page Spanish R823 working translation covers all 81 declared source units, Papers 01-43, all 31 lecture-book sections, and retained terminal material. Its declared source-reconciliation gate passed, but this is not native-language or peer-review certification.

Interslavic: two directly readable working-translation PDFs expose 221 canonical Latin-script units as a 529-page reader and 221 paired Cyrillic-script units as a 552-page reader. File 11 groups the complete current TeX bodies, all individual PDFs, unit mapping, support metadata, normalization preimages/diffs/ledgers, build logs, scripts, and visual-QA evidence. Orthography Tranche 002A changed 146 files; exact lexical Tranche 002B changed 92 files. Both transformations passed idempotence checks and preserved held or unreviewed forms. The archive pass compiled all 442 canonical units with no missing-character or box-overflow diagnostics; four symmetric amsmath bracket-group notices remain in Paper 06 sections 02-03.

Other material: the record retains bounded Arabic and Iranian-Persian Paper 06 openings, a complete-work Indonesian Paper 36 working translation, the earlier Paper 06 Slavic tranche, German source packages, source-repair/audit material, and grouped multilingual checkpoints.

CJK direct readers: eight directly visible PDFs expose complete Noether Papers 26 and 36 in Simplified Chinese, generic Traditional Chinese, Japanese, and Korean. Exact editable TeX and audit evidence are preserved in file 09. The PDFs passed independent rebuild, visual, manifest, and public-readback hash checks, but they do not have external native-language signoff. The Traditional Chinese texts are generic adaptations rather than Taiwan- or Hong-Kong-localized editions.

Status caveat: these are substantial machine-produced working editions and translations. They are not a critical edition, native-language or community certification, peer review, publication-grade final edition, complete multilingual synchronization, or a guarantee that every word, formula, diagram, and symbol has received independent human source verification. Build and render checks establish artifact integrity and bounded change control; they do not establish linguistic or mathematical correctness.

GitHub: corrections, source comparisons, LaTeX fixes, and translation improvements can be suggested through issues or pull requests at https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/modern-latex-manuscripts.
notes: Reader-first public surface: R823 German source-control, RA10 and bounded R823 English, 473-page Spanish R823, 529/552-page Interslavic Latin/Cyrillic readers, and direct complete Papers 26/36 in Simplified Chinese, generic Traditional Chinese, Japanese, and Korean. Not a critical edition, native-language certification, peer review, or complete source-level multilingual synchronization.
